metadata.note: El Paso and Northeastern system (EP&NE Railroad of Texas, EP&NE Railway, El Paso and Rock Island, Dawson Railway, Alamogordo and Sacramento Mountain), its 1908-1924 operator the El Paso and Southwestern, and the Southern Pacific from Nov 1 1924: El Paso - Carrizozo - Santa Rosa - Tucumcari main line and the Dawson, Capitan and Cloudcroft (Cox Canon, Russia) branches, New Mexico and Texas. Drawn exactly to the research report's drawable: fields. Research report: research/branches/el_paso_and_northeastern_railway.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 splits at Apr 1 1908 (all five system companies leased to the El Paso and Southwestern; ICC valuation reports) and Nov 1 1924 (Southern Pacific control Oct 31 1924). The Jul 1 1905 Phelps Dodge purchase was a stock purchase - the ICC says each company operated its own property until Mar 31 1908 - so it is NOT a split (some sources word it as an EP&SW purchase; recorded in not_yet_sourced). The EP&RI, Dawson Railway and A&SM were legally separate 'own organization' operators to 1908 but ran as one EP&NE system under common management, so all pre-1908 features carry company 'El Paso and Northeastern' and one colour (a judgment call recommended by the report). Colours: El Paso and Northeastern #3D7A6E and El Paso and Southwestern #B3592B are new; a script confirmed no other company in data/ uses either (a future El Paso and Southwestern layer should reuse #B3592B). Southern Pacific #C1272D was pulled programmatically from the existing 'Southern Pacific Railroad' features.
metadata.existing_layer_check: crip-golden-state-route (chicago_rock_island_pacific.geojson, company 'Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific / Southern Pacific (joint)') draws the Golden State over this same track 1902-1968 and is not edited here. The report flags a defect in it: its 1902-1948 segment says the SP ran El Paso - Santa Rosa from 1902 and that the Rock Island used leased SP track to Tucumcari, whereas El Paso - Santa Rosa was EP&NE (to Mar 1908) then EP&SW (to Oct 1924) and Santa Rosa - Tucumcari was Rock Island track used by the EP&SW/SP under trackage rights. That feature's maintainers should decide on the fix. The SP-era main line is drawn here as its own SP feature (sp-el-paso-tucumcari), as the report recommends, because the SP's own trains (the Imperial) ran there and Rule 4 wants SP's colour on that track.
omitted: El Paso and Northeastern on Santa Rosa - Tucumcari (report [3a]): no EP&NE-train year proven - drawable NONE.
Southern Pacific on the Capitan Branch ([5c]): no SP-era passenger year confirmed (1932 letter is a working timetable); abandonment 1943.
Southern Pacific beyond Cloudcroft ([7c], [8c]) and El Paso and Northeastern Cox Canon - Russia ([8a]): unproven.
Golden State Limited ([9]): already drawn by crip-golden-state-route.
Capitan - North Capitan / Coalora extension (1.12 mi, 1901): not a separate drawable block in the report; the Capitan Branch is drawn to the east end of the mapped grade.

Freight only (Rule 1): Jarilla / Jarilla - Zora mining spur; logging railroads around Cloudcroft and beyond Russia; freight afterlives of the Capitan (to 1943), Cloudcroft (to 1947) and Dawson (to 1961) branches; the main line after Apr 8 1968.
metadata.freight_only_audit: No freight-only content drawn. Capitan and Dawson are coal branches that carried public passenger trains (1900/1905 Guides, 1910 and 1924 EP&SW timetables, the 1933 SP memo) and are drawn for those years only.
not_yet_sourced: epne-el-paso-carrizozo: START [OPEN] at 1900. Opened to Alamogordo 1898 (Jun 15 1898 per the El Paso railroad timeline, uncited) / operated from Jan 1 1899 (ICC). A dated 1898 or 1899 timetable or 'first passenger train' newspaper item would move it earlier.
epne-dawson-branch: START [OPEN] at 1905; line operated from Jul 1 1903.
epne-capitan-branch: START [OPEN] at 1900; completion to Capitan Aug 3 vs Sep 29 1899 (sources differ).
epne-cloudcroft-branch and epne-cloudcroft-cox-canon: START [OPEN] at 1902; reached Cloudcroft 1900.
epsw-santa-rosa-tucumcari: START [OPEN] at 1910; EP&NE/EP&SW-system trains may have used the Rock Island line from Jul 1903. ICC says trackage rights, some sources say lease (conflict).
epsw-capitan-branch: END [OPEN] at 1924; real passenger end somewhere 1924-1943.
epsw-cloudcroft-cox-canon: END [OPEN] at 1924; whether trains ran beyond Cloudcroft after 1924 is unknown.
epsw-cox-canon-russia: START [OPEN] at 1910 and END [OPEN] at 1924.
sp-dawson-branch: END [OPEN] at 1933 (SP memo); Feb 1952 Table 93 exists with train 974 but no recoverable times. Needs an SP Rio Grande Division timetable or ICC FD 18641 / 21591.
sp-cloudcroft-branch: END conflict, March 1937 vs 1938; 1937 drawn.
Phelps Dodge purchase Jul 1 1905: sources word it as an EP&SW purchase of the EP&NE; if an employee timetable or annual report shows trains in the EP&SW name from 1905, the 1908 split moves to 1905.

Geometry: Cloudcroft branch traced 31% short (a 5.47-mi chord past High Rolls and Wooten, plus other straight legs); Capitan branch 7.08-mi chord across the Walnut switchback; Cox Canon - Russia mostly straight and Cox Canon's position is computed, not located; Russia rests on one OSM polygon.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt): Tables 8/11, 93 and the CRI&P connection table

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 143.8 mi against 144.7 mi documented (Fowler route 26 mileposts; ICC 19.943 + 124.833 = 144.8). No straight-line leg; every mile routed by opstrace.py over live OSM track: 9.4 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator='Southern Pacific Railroad' (UP Carrizozo Subdivision), the rest on untagged active UP track (Carrizozo Subdivision). segments.note: El Paso and Northeastern main line, El Paso - Alamogordo - Tularosa - Carrizozo (EP&NE RR of Texas to the state line, EP&NE Ry beyond). START [OPEN]: 1900 is the first PROVEN passenger year - Fowler's 1900 Official Guide letters on Carrizozo ('Carrizosa 1900G') and Oscura ('Malagra 1900G'). The line opened to Alamogordo in 1898 (Jun 15 1898 per the El Paso railroad timeline; ICC: EP&NE Ry operated by its own organization from Jan 1 1899) and reached Capitan in 1899, so service very likely began earlier, but no earlier year is confirmed - do not extend without evidence. From Nov 1902 the line also carried the Golden State Limited (drawn separately by crip-golden-state-route). Phelps Dodge bought the system's stock Jul 1 1905, but the ICC valuation says the EP&NE companies operated their own property until Mar 31 1908; the El Paso and Southwestern lease took effect Apr 1 1908 (next feature). headway_min is an estimate, not from a timetable.

segments.note: El Paso and Rock Island Railway (an EP&NE system company, operated by its own organization under EP&NE management; drawn in the system's colour), Carrizozo - Ancho - Corona - Duran - Vaughn - Pastura - Santa Rosa, meeting the Rock Island's westward extension at Santa Rosa to complete the Golden State Route. First section opened Feb 1 1902 (ICC; El Paso Herald Feb 1 1902); whole line turned over for operation Apr 1 1903. 1902 rests on the Golden State Limited's first stops at El Paso on Nov 4 1902 (El Paso Herald Nov 5 1902), which can only have come over this line; that first season was winter-only (to May 1903). Ends at the EP&SW lease, Apr 1 1908. headway_min is an estimate, not from a timetable.

segments.note: Southern Pacific operation of the former EP&SW line El Paso - Alamogordo - Carrizozo - Vaughn - Santa Rosa, and SP trackage rights over the Rock Island's Santa Rosa - Tucumcari line, from Nov 1 1924 (control acquired Oct 31 1924). The SP's own trains here included the Imperial (No. 39/40; off in 1967) alongside the joint Golden State (No. 3/4) - the Feb 1952 Official Guide shows both with times (Lv Tucumcari 9:39 AM / 8:10 PM, Ar El Paso 3:15 PM / 2:45 AM). The joint through Golden State is ALSO drawn separately, by the crip-golden-state-route feature in chicago_rock_island_pacific.geojson; this feature carries Rule 4's SP colour for the operator of the El Paso - Tucumcari track. Every SP-era passenger train found here was a through train; no SP local was found. Ends with the Golden State's last run, Apr 8 1968, which ended passenger service to Tucumcari. Freight continues (Union Pacific since 1996). headway_min (two trains each way daily, as in Feb 1952) is a single-year figure applied to the whole span - an estimate for other years.
